nodes.label: Pruned-Mirror Handoff Closeout Plan
nodes.rationale: Closes HANDOFF.md: six shipped prose defects, four deferred code fixes (lock, streaming object sweep, utf-8 git output, cache permissions), two uncovered lines, and the docs. Every change stays inside ensure_pruned_mirror and its neighbours; all git behavior claims were measured on darwin/APFS/git 2.50.1 during plan review.

nodes.label: Mutation anchors constrain how the code may be edited
nodes.rationale: mutation_check.py matches exact source substrings including leading indentation and reports STALE ANCHOR otherwise. Six anchors live inside ensure_pruned_mirror's body, which is why the lock is added by extracting the body into a helper rather than wrapping it in a `with` -- re-indenting the region would stale all six.

nodes.label: _build_pruned_mirror as a seam, not a decomposition
nodes.rationale: The body moves verbatim and unre-indented so every mutation anchor inside it survives byte-for-byte; inlining it back 'for tidiness' stales all six. Its docstring says so, because the wrapper's comment is not where someone editing the body looks.

nodes.label: One flock per repo slug
nodes.rationale: Closes three readers: the mirror fetch path (clone writes HEAD early so a second process fetches into a half-populated clone), the prune build-and-publish, and materialize's run-tree clone (the publish rmtree's the directory that clone is reading). Per slug, not per (repo, base_sha), because both keys share one source mirror and one sweep namespace. flock self-conflicts across two fds in one process, so the acquisitions must not nest. The lock file is never unlinked -- removing one another process holds open silently breaks exclusion for every later acquirer.

nodes.label: _commits_outside streams one past its sample
nodes.rationale: Buffering the whole --batch-all-objects listing was 659 KB on pruned click and ~229 MB extrapolated to a 5M-object monorepo, for a message that prints three names. Reading ONE past the sample is what lets the message distinguish 'exactly N' from 'more than N' -- 3 outside commits (a ref-sweep miss) and 30,000 (a gc that did nothing) are different diagnoses, and absence-is-recorded forbids rendering them identically.

nodes.label: _git decodes pinned utf-8 with replacement
nodes.rationale: text=True decodes with the process locale and errors='strict', so one non-UTF-8 byte in git output -- or LC_ALL=C on a CI runner -- raised UnicodeDecodeError naming neither the repo nor the task. The old 'a mangled ref gets deleted, the safe direction' claim was measured false: the ref sweep deletes by decoded name and update-ref --stdin exits 0 on a nonexistent ref, so the real ref survives and _verify_pruned's object sweep refuses the mirror. Loud refusal, not a leak.

nodes.label: Published mirror keeps mkdtemp's 0700
nodes.rationale: The fix is a deletion, not a chmod: the rmtree existed on a claim that clone 'tolerates an empty target only if it does not exist', measured false -- git 2.50.1 clones into an existing empty directory and keeps its mode. Without it the clone recreates the directory under the umask and os.replace publishes a world-readable cache permanently. The test pins umask(0) so the verdict is the repository's, not the laptop's.

nodes.label: A damaged prune cache rebuilds rather than raises
nodes.rationale: Raising left the damaged entry on disk, unmaterializable until an operator deleted it by hand -- three identical TaskErrors measured, with a message that reads like a prune bug and no instruction to delete anything. The rebuild's own post-condition on the tmp it just built still raises and still gates the rename: refusing a prune this code built is a code defect, refusing one it found on disk is a cache defect, and only the second is recoverable.

nodes.label: Publish TaskError must not name reclaimed paths
nodes.rationale: The message said 'the build itself succeeded and is at {tmp}' while the finally-block rmtree reclaims tmp as the exception propagates. Rewording rather than preserving tmp is right: tmp and dest are siblings so EXDEV is impossible and ENOSPC is the live failure, where stranding a full mirror makes the problem worse. It also must not tell the operator to act on dest, which on the second os.replace has itself been renamed aside.

nodes.label: The base_sha guard exists for a NAMED failure, not a vacuous pass
nodes.rationale: The shipped claim -- that without the cat-file -e guard _commits_outside passes vacuously on an empty store -- is false: _ancestors runs rev-list under check=True and raises first. What the caller loses is the message, since _git's generic exit-128 line names neither the mirror nor the fact that this is a cache defect. The same false claim shipped in three places at once.

nodes.label: The stale-tmp sweep skips an unstatable entry
nodes.rationale: The sweep stats entries it did not create in a cache directory shared by every repo, so an entry can vanish between the glob and the stat when another invocation reclaims it first. That OSError must mean 'skip', never 'fail the build': the sweep only reclaims disk, and a build that dies on someone else's leftover turns a janitor into a single point of failure.
